title: Bounded derived smooth base change
statement:
Use the coefficient conventions [sbc-def-coefficient-conventions]: $\Lambda$ is a finite commutative ring, $N$ is a positive integer, $(N:\Lambda)=0$, and $N$ is invertible on $S$ (equivalently its image is a unit in $\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$). In a cartesian square [sbc-def-base-change-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X&\xleftarrow{h}&Y\\
f\downarrow&&\downarrow e\\
S&\xleftarrow{g}&T,
\end{array}
$$
assume $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For every $K\in\Dbc(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], the canonical derived exchange
$$
\operatorname{BC}_{f,g}(K):Lf^*Rg_*K\longrightarrow Rh_*Le^*K
$$
of [sbc-def-base-change-map] is an isomorphism in the ambient unbounded category $D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. No boundedness or constructibility of its two endpoints is asserted.

proof.text: Extract the lower cohomological bound $a$ from [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The standard derived-category criterion `DerivedCategory.isGE_iff` proves $K\in D^{\ge a}$, so form the bounded-below object $K^+=\langle K,a\rangle$. The chosen pullback isomorphism and its projection equations give `IsPullback e h g f` by `IsPullback.of_iso_pullback` and symmetry. No constructibility conversion or bound on either output is needed.

By [sbc-def-coefficient-conventions], $N>0$, $(N:\Lambda)=0$, and $N$ is a unit on $S$. For every sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules, including every $H^j(K^+)$, `Scheme.IsTorsionSheafOfInvertibleOrder.of_natCast_eq_zero` supplies the invertible-order torsion structure: on each geometric stalk, $Nx=(N:\Lambda)x=0$. Apply the already proved upstream theorem `Etale.isIso_baseChange_app_of_smooth_of_isTorsionSheafOfInvertibleOrder` to $K^+$ and the exchanged square. Its smooth and qcqs hypotheses are exactly the given ones. This packaged theorem reduces to [sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] on sheaves and extends it by triangulated truncation devissage and the cohomological truncation criterion; it directly handles ModuleCat coefficients. Thus the canonical bounded-below module exchange at $K^+$ is invertible, with no new theorem or sorry.

The source-library equality `baseChange_eq_derivedBaseChangeMapPlus` identifies that bounded-below map with `derivedBaseChangeMapPlus`. The proved generic module comparison `isIso_derivedBaseChangeMap_app_ι_obj_iff` identifies its invertibility with that of the exact specified ambient map [sbc-def-base-change-map], evaluated at $K=(\iota K^+)$. This comparison uses the canonical inverse-image and right-derived-direct-image endpoint isomorphisms and full faithfulness of $D^+\to D$. Apply its reverse implication to the isomorphism of Step 2. This proves the unchanged target arrow directly, without forgetting coefficients or using the abelian spectral-sequence machinery.
